chunks: Everything submits to Him and everything exists by Him. He is the satisfaction of every poor, dignity of the low, energy for the weak and shelter for the oppressed. Whoever speaks, He hears his speaking, and whoever keeps quit, He knows his secret. On Him is the livelihood of everyone who lives, and to Him returns whoever dies.
ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of power and knowledge described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali articulates the comprehensive nature of Divine Omnipotence (Qudra), highlighting that every creature's existence and sustenance are entirely dependent on God's will. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on God's absolute self-sufficiency contrasted with creation's inherent neediness, serving as a source of comfort for the distressed and a reminder of ultimate accountability.
